correctness.rationale: Under the stated convention a repeated occurrence is net iff both available one-letter extensions are unique, treating missing boundary extensions as unique. If p is the primitive-root length, equality of two cyclic rotations would give a proper cyclic period dividing p. Hence long factors can occur at only one phase. All occurring strings of length at most p repeat at starts r and r+p for some r<p, within the first 3p positions; this excludes net occurrences of lengths below p. For length at least p an occurrence class at positive phase has at least two identical left extensions whenever repeated. At phase zero with at least three occurrences, all positive starts have repeated left extensions, and the zero start's right extension repeats at p. With just starts 0 and p, the positive start is the only possible source of its left extension. The zero start's right extension then occurs only once precisely when the second occurrence runs to the right boundary; otherwise both right extensions repeat. This gives exactly the two occurrences of v^(e-1), including p=1. Independently, /workspace/audit-replay/2.py used forward and reverse longest common prefixes of suffix pairs to derive net intervals from equal longest-repeat lengths on both sides. Output 2.txt records 9332 primitive-power cases at exponents 3,4,5,7 (binary roots through length 9, ternary through 6, four-symbol through 4) and the four asserted square intervals. The tests corroborate rather than replace the proof.
